page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.2xlarge is a burstable, shared-core virtual instance designed for cost-conscious, variable-load applications. Powered by the Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance exposes 8 virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance operates without bundled local NVMe storage and includes no dedicated hardware GPUs, requiring external network block storage volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark data reflects the burstable CPU allocation profile. Single-core compute scores lean toward the lower tiers, as demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1039.0 and a stress-ng single-core result of 1303.28. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics perform within median ranges across shared instances, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 10087.86, a Geekbench multi-core score of 4827.0, and 9.62 million operations per second in Redis SET throughput. Memory operations show stable throughput with large uncached read bandwidth reaching 61.66 GB/sec and write bandwidth achieving 33.94 GB/sec.

Given its credit-based compute model and 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, sustained CPU-heavy operations such as LLM inference or continuous compression exhibit reduced efficiency. However, the density of 32 GB of memory paired with 8 burstable vCPUs offers qualitative cost efficiency for intermittent workloads. Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.2xlarge is well aligned with environments such as medium-scale development servers, staging environments, periodic batch processing, low-traffic web applications, and internal database replicas that do not demand sustained maximum CPU utilization.

No local persistent storage or hardware GPUs are bundled with the configuration, relying instead on network block volumes. Benchmark evaluations show moderate multi-core throughput, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 4827.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 10087.86, alongside 9.62 million Redis SET operations per second, while single-core metrics remain in lower benchmark percentiles due to burstable scheduling. The resource profile provides budget-conscious capacity suited for low-to-medium traffic web hosting, staging and testing environments, and asynchronous batch workers.
